pathogens.why: Disseminated TB reflects hematogenous spread of M. tuberculosis, classically producing miliary lung nodules and multi-organ involvement (liver, spleen, bone marrow, CNS), and is disproportionately seen in immunocompromised hosts (HIV, malnutrition, immunosuppressive therapy) where the presentation can be especially non-specific, contributing to diagnostic delay.

investigations.why: Classic miliary pattern (diffuse small nodules) supports the diagnosis, though it may be subtle or absent early.

investigations.test: Blood culture for mycobacteria (if available) and AFB smear of any accessible fluid/tissue
investigations.why: May provide microbiological confirmation; mycobacterial blood culture has reasonable yield in disseminated disease, particularly in HIV co-infection.

investigations.test: Liver or bone marrow biopsy (if hepatosplenomegaly/cytopenias and other tests inconclusive)
investigations.why: Can provide histological confirmation (caseating granulomas, AFB on staining) when other less invasive tests are unrevealing.
Essential given the strong association between disseminated TB and immunosuppression, with direct treatment implications.
Screens for concurrent CNS involvement, which would extend treatment duration.
